record_identity.title: OSS-Fuzz-Gen evaluation exposed misleading crashes from invalid AI-generated test drivers

incident_identity.historical_event_name: OSS-Fuzz-Gen false-positive crash evaluation reported in FalseCrashReducer
incident_identity.date_basis: Section 5.1 places the experiments between July and September 2025. The structured year preserves the known year; the narrower month interval is retained in the narrative. No exact start or end day is inferred.

summary: Between July and September 2025, researchers evaluated AI-generated fuzz drivers in OSS-Fuzz-Gen using Gemini 2.5 Pro and 1,555 benchmark functions from 336 projects. Some drivers violated internal functions’ calling requirements and produced crashes that were not reachable through normal application entry points. The existing crash analyser also labelled some driver errors as program errors. The researchers added function constraints and contextual crash validation, reducing spurious results. Their paper, published on 2 October 2025, reports roughly 70% false-positive crashes, although its prose and table assign the totals differently. No production outage or customer loss is reported.

vigil_assessment.factual_basis: The originating paper provides a concrete libraw driver example, benchmark setup and aggregate results. Sections 2 and 3 distinguish an invalid harness invocation from a reachable application defect. Section 5.2.3 describes program-error classifications later rejected by contextual validation. Section 5.1 dates the cloud experiments and names Gemini 2.5 Pro. Section 3.3 and Table 2 disagree on which configuration produced the 4,835 total; the difference is retained rather than resolved by inference. The repository listing does not independently reconcile the data.
vigil_assessment.governance_interpretation: A crash artefact received more diagnostic weight than its calling context justified. The immediate defect could lie in the generated harness rather than the tested application. Contextual feasibility therefore matters before a crash becomes evidence of an application vulnerability.
vigil_assessment.significance_to_cam: A testing system can create misleading evidence when it changes the conditions under which a function is called. Validating the test setup is separate from reproducing the crash or attributing a defect to the application.
assessment_boundaries: This record concerns the July–September 2025 evaluation, not every deployment or output of OSS-Fuzz or OSS-Fuzz-Gen.

The paper prose describes 4,835 crashes with about 70% false positives. Table 2 lists 5,080 baseline crashes with 3,583 false positives and 4,835 constrained crashes with 3,390 false positives. These totals must not be silently conflated.
The table contains apparent formatting or aggregation anomalies. Exact reconciled counts require author clarification or a separate raw-data audit.
A false positive means the crash is not feasible from a valid application entry point under the stated model; the harness itself can still crash.
No affected maintainer, production vulnerability report, outage, customer loss or physical consequence is established from the aggregate evaluation.
Gemini 2.5 Pro is reported for these experiments. Results are not assumed to generalise to other models or software domains.
The public artifact repository was inspected only at its top-level listing. Its raw datasets were not independently audited.

clauses.source_anchor: Sections 2.1, 3.3 and 5.2.3: invalid calling context and program-error classification
clauses.source_paraphrase: Generated drivers violated function preconditions. Some resulting crashes were labelled program errors and subsequently rejected by context-aware validation.
clauses.recovered_invariant_interpretation: A crash must be attributable to a feasible application execution before it is relied upon as evidence of an application defect.

taxonomy_relationships.rationale: AI-generated drivers called internal functions outside valid calling conditions. The resulting crash artefacts were treated as program-error evidence even though later context validation identified additional driver errors. The crash was real in the constructed harness, but its interpretation as a reachable application defect lacked the assurance required for defect triage.
